profile.reading:
This Fort Worth property carries the Novartis name in the registry because of the site's history with Alcon, the eye care company that operated as a Novartis division for close to a decade before becoming an independent, publicly traded company again in 2019. Alcon Laboratories built its global headquarters and a cluster of manufacturing, distribution and office buildings along the South Freeway corridor in south Fort Worth, and this address at 6601 South Freeway sits within that same corridor. Novartis acquired majority control of Alcon in 2010 and completed a full buyout in 2011, folding Alcon's Fort Worth campus into the Novartis corporate structure until the 2019 spinoff returned Alcon to independent ownership. Whether this specific building still carries any Novartis affiliation today, or reverted fully to Alcon or another tenant after the spinoff, is not established in the sources reviewed for this page.

Neither Novartis nor Alcon publishes facility level detail, such as floor plans, server room square footage, power capacity or cooling design, for individual buildings on the South Freeway campus. Large pharmaceutical and life sciences companies of this size typically operate information technology infrastructure as a mix of on site server rooms supporting manufacturing and quality control systems, leased colocation space, and public cloud services, rather than as a single named data center open to public description. Nothing in the public record singles out 6601 South Freeway as a standalone data center distinct from ordinary corporate or manufacturing support computing space.

Tarrant County property and permit records place the parcel in a commercial and industrial area, consistent with the surrounding South Freeway corridor's mix of pharmaceutical manufacturing, warehousing and office space, but no permit filing, zoning case or trade press coverage identified for this address describes a purpose built data hall, generator plant or dedicated cooling infrastructure. No expansion announcement, outage report or construction filing tied specifically to this building has been found.

In short, this address is best understood as a Fort Worth facility connected to Novartis's ownership history in the region, most plausibly through the former Alcon campus, rather than as a data center whose technical specifications are publicly documented. Readers looking for verified power, capacity or tenancy figures for this address will not find them published by either company.
